title: Right Lower Quadrant Pain Variant 7

patient.name: Betty Hernandez
patient.initial_statement: My stomach started hurting this morning around my belly button. Over the afternoon, it moved down to my lower right side and is hurting so much now.

symptoms: Migrating abdominal pain: starting in periumbilical area, shifting to RLQ
Nausea, lost appetite (anorexia) since this morning
Pain is severe, throbbing, and worsened by walking or jumping
allergies: No known drug or food allergies
review_of_systems: Cardiovascular: pulse rate is 103 bpm, no active chest pain except as noted.

patient_beliefs: I hope this is just a temporary strain that will pass.
I've been under a lot of stress with my job.
I'm terrified this might be something permanent or fatal.
patient_goals: Determine the core cause of these symptoms.
Verify whether there is emergency intervention required.
Get diagnostic results explained to me step by step.

examinations.name: General Physical Examination
examinations.result: Alert, looks flushed and uncomfortable. Lies still with knees slightly bent.

examinations.name: Cardiovascular Examination
examinations.result: Regular heart rate (103 bpm), normal cardiovascular sounds.

examinations.name: Abdominal Examination
examinations.result: Soft, guarded. Exquisite tenderness in the Right Lower Quadrant (RLQ) at McBurney's point. Positive rebound tenderness and positive Rovsing's sign.

investigations.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
investigations.result: Normal sinus rhythm, regular rate 72 bpm, no ST/T abnormalities.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
investigations.result: WBC: 14.8 x10^9/L (Elevated; Normal 4.0-11.0), Neutrophils: 85% (Elevated), Hb: 14.0 g/dL.
investigations.interpretation: Leukocytosis with left shift, highly indicative of acute bacterial inflammation/infection.

investigations.name: Serum Electrolytes Panel
investigations.interpretation: Serum electrolytes are within normal range.

investigations.name: Chest X-ray (CXR)
investigations.result: Both lungs are hypolucent, no vascular congestion or consolidation.

investigations.name: CT Angiography of Chest
investigations.result: Normal caliber aorta, no luminal narrowing, no dissection flap visible.

investigations.name: CT Scan of Head (cranial assessment)
investigations.result: No acute hemorrhage, infarct, or midline shifts found in cranial structures.
investigations.interpretation: Normal CT Scan of the Head.

investigations.name: CT Scan of Abdomen & Pelvis
investigations.result: CT of the Abdomen/Pelvis shows a dilated, thick-walled appendix measuring 10.5 mm in diameter, surrounding fat stranding, hyperenhancement of the wall, and trace fluid in the right lower quadrant.
investigations.interpretation: Acute appendicitis. Surgical consultation is recommended.

investigations.name: Urinalysis and Urine Culture
investigations.result: Clear yellow appearance, negative nitrite, negative leukocyte esterase.
investigations.interpretation: Urinalysis is clear of infection signs.

investigations.name: Duplex Vascular Leg Ultrasound
investigations.result: Normal patency of left and right femoral veins with complete color Doppler signal.

red_flags: Severe acute presentation requiring advanced imaging or intervention
